conditions: Classes are read as data. No vendor class is loaded or initialized.
A serialized node is resolved by the declared target descriptor of the relationship that references it; the root is the module-contents class of the module file.

Initialization entries are the constructor, the base methods that static factories call on a fresh object, the base serialization hooks, and the instance methods that the module factory closure calls on the module class.

Reachability follows this-calls inside the class chain, super calls from the named class, and calls on helper objects that are not document objects, at most two hops away. Calls on other document objects are not followed; those objects have their own closure.

A creation counts when the created class is a concrete document object and the creating body, or the init body that receives it from a helper, passes it to a call on this or on a document object whose parameter type is one of its ancestors, or adds it to a collection.
A document object created on an init path without such a store is a helper object. It is not in the set, but its own init closure is followed for children stored into the tree.
The set is an over-approximation of the runtime tree for the fixed Amplify module: a conditional creation on an init path is included even when the data does not take it.
The disposal chain compares body contracts modulo renaming. It does not run any body.
